comments.note: MysqlDumpBackupService.cs: The MySQL option file content is written as [client]\npassword=<value>\n. If the password contains special characters (e.g., #, quotes, backslashes), MySQL option file parsing rules may misinterpret the value. Consider quoting the password value or escaping special characters in a follow-up work package.

MysqlDumpBackupService.cs: The temp .cnf file is written to Path.GetTempPath() with only a random filename as access control. On Windows, %TEMP% is user-scoped which limits exposure, but restricting ACLs via FileSecurity (noted as a stretch goal in the WP) would provide defense-in-depth. The WP explicitly documented this as out of scope.

MysqlDumpBackupService.cs: BackupAsync restructuring moved psi and Process creation inside the try block and captured exitCode/stderrText as local variables before the finally. The code is correct but the variable initialization (exitCode=0, stderrText=string.Empty) before try could be confusing. The pattern is idiomatic for C# async/finally and clear in context.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (MysqlDumpBackupService.cs, MysqlDumpBackupServiceTests.cs). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 2 Low findings noted. Security sign-off: PASS. The WP correctly eliminates password exposure in process argument lists by routing credentials through a short-lived GUID-named temp .cnf file, cleaned up unconditionally in a finally block. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed.

comments.note:
Low — A03/Injection (self-injection only): MysqlDumpBackupService.cs — the .cnf file content is written as '[client]
password={raw_value}
' with no newline escaping. A password containing a literal newline character (e.g., 'secret
user=injected') could inject additional MySQL option file keys. Risk is low because the password originates from the user's own stored connection settings (IDatabaseConnectionStore), not from untrusted external input. Remediation (future WP): strip or reject newline characters from password values before writing to the .cnf file, or quote/escape the value per MySQL option file syntax.

Low — A02/Cryptographic Failures (defence-in-depth, out of scope per WP): MysqlDumpBackupService.cs — the temp .cnf file is created via File.WriteAllTextAsync with no explicit FileSecurity ACLs restricting read access to the current user only. On Windows, %TEMP% is user-scoped which adequately limits exposure in practice. Setting restrictive ACLs via FileSecurity would provide additional defence-in-depth. Documented as a stretch goal and explicitly out of scope for this WP.

Info — A02 (pre-existing, noted for awareness): MysqlDumpBackupService.cs — the MySQL option file special-character issue previously flagged by Developer and QA agents. Passwords containing '#' (MySQL comment character), unescaped quotes, or backslashes may be silently misread by mysqldump's option file parser, causing backup failures. Not a security regression from WP-006 (password was previously exposed on the command line in plaintext). Should be addressed in a follow-up WP by quoting or escaping the password value.

summary: Reviewed MysqlDumpBackupService.cs and MysqlDumpBackupServiceTests.cs against all Review Dimensions.

Credential file strategy is architecturally sound: string? credentialsFilePath = null initialized before try, written inside try, deleted unconditionally in finally with best-effort catch. The null-check guard in finally prevents double-delete on WriteAllTextAsync failure.

catch (Exception ex) when (ex is not OperationCanceledException) guard is technically redundant — C# evaluates catch blocks in order so OperationCanceledException would never reach this block — but the explicit guard serves as a self-documenting intent marker. Non-blocking.

Process lifecycle on cancellation: Process.Dispose() does not kill the mysqldump process. When CopyToAsync is cancelled the FileStream is disposed (closing the stdout pipe), causing mysqldump to fail on its next write and exit naturally. This is correct OS-level behavior but worth documenting as an implicit contract.

BuildStartInfo correctly places --defaults-extra-file as the first ArgumentList entry per mysqldump requirements. All connection field values are discrete ArgumentList entries with zero string concatenation, correctly eliminating shell injection.

10 unit tests provide comprehensive coverage of argument structure, redirection flags, null-connection edge cases, and BackupAsync early-exit paths. All pass. PASS — no blocking issues, no fix-forward changes applied.

comments.note: catch (Exception ex) when (ex is not OperationCanceledException) — the when guard is redundant since C# evaluates catch clauses in order and OperationCanceledException is already consumed by the preceding catch block. The guard is not harmful and makes intent explicit, but a future cleanup could simplify this to catch (Exception ex) for readability. Not a blocker.

Process lifecycle on cancellation: mysqldump is not explicitly killed on cancellation — the code relies on pipe-broken behavior (FileStream disposed → stdout write fails → mysqldump exits). This is correct in practice on all supported OS platforms but constitutes an implicit contract with the OS. Consider documenting this in the XML doc comment for BackupAsync as a future improvement.
